Ln.bar_b_note: Warm meadow palette helps, but the frozen creatures, the cramped HUD-heavy framing and flat lighting with no sky or atmosphere sink it.

St.bar_b_note: B's glowing lightning-fur wolf approaches the style bar, but A's faint material breakdown and B's head-down faint pose are below a shipping finish.

Co.bar_b_note: Hit markers and lilac telegraph slabs bury rigid creatures, and there is no light or atmosphere to carry the meadow.

Io.bar_b_note: A top-down camera on a uniform grass carpet shrinks the fighters to dots, with no horizon, sky or depth.

Zq.bar_b_note: Muddy brown forest with no storm sky, debug HUD over the frame, flat magenta telegraphs and (B) the camera inside foliage.

Aj.bar_b_note: Only the small creature reacts; the badger stays in its idle pose, and B's huge lilac dodge arc hides the fight.

Af.bar_b_note: A clean, appealing villager with readable eyes, but too glossy and cartoon against naturalistic Palworld/Valheim-level finish.

Az.bar_b_note: A's site-specific aftermaths read well, but blurry stretched ground, low-poly repeated trees and flat light sink the finish; B leaves enemy banners standing.

top_changes.change: Give every creature (especially the armoured badger) real hit-flinch, stagger, dodge-lean and faint animations and grounded faint poses instead of idle-pose holds

Reframe the combat camera (no top-down or inside-foliage shots, keep both fighters large) and replace flat lilac/magenta telegraph slabs and oversized hit rings with smaller physical effects; strip debug HUD panels
Add Valheim-level lighting and atmosphere (sky, fog depth, sun shafts; Stormwood purple storm sky and lightning) and sharpen the blurry, stretched ground textures
